note: A material limit is a question, not a delivery defect: the severity contract separates what the MATERIAL did not carry from what the DELIVERY fails, and both budgets are re-set from the measured distribution across this leg.

claims.statement: The severity list's `gap` entry now reads "the DELIVERY fails a contract requirement: the bytes are PRESENT and do not do what the criterion says, or something the criterion requires is absent FROM THE DELIVERY", and rules the material limit out in the same entry — "Bytes the MATERIAL did not carry are NOT this — a patch the stated budget cut is the material's own limit, not the delivery's defect, and filing it here routes a REWORK for something the delivery may well satisfy. Raise those as \"uncertain\"." That last clause is the measured failure named where the reader meets it: on 12/27 a cut file was filed as a gap and the rule answered rework, twice. Pinned by a test asserting both halves, so the old ambiguous sentence cannot be read as the whole rule.

`uncertain` now admits SETTLEMENT as well as localization — "a real concern you cannot SETTLE: either you cannot localize it to a file and line, or the MATERIAL did not carry the bytes that would settle it (name the file the change map shows and the cut states it dropped)" — and the material's boundary section says the same thing at the point of use: "Raise any of them as `uncertain` and say what you would need — NOT as `gap`: a gap is a defect in the DELIVERY, and these are limits of the MATERIAL, which the delivery may well satisfy. The change map above is complete, so a file whose hunks were cut is still NAMED: point at it by name." The two halves agree, and both are pinned by tests that read the BUILT material rather than the source text.

Both budgets are re-set from measurement over this leg's 25 nodes, with the figures stated beside them. DIFF_CHARS 60,000 → 180,000: the old value contradicted its own comment, which recorded 12/08's patch as 137,547 chars while claiming "the number below carries a delivery of that size". Ten deliveries exceed 60,000 (05 604,779 · 22 165,281 · 08 138,646 · 09 110,058 · 27 102,495 · 11 91,263 · 10 75,922 · 12 74,399 · 07 65,639 · 06 65,440) — a third of the leg, not an edge case. 180,000 carries all of them but 12/05, which overflows any budget that still fits a context window. STAT_CHARS 4,000 → 12,000: the widest map in the leg is 12/05's at 4,047, so "a file whose hunks were cut is always NAMED rather than invisible" was false by 47 chars on the one delivery whose patch is cut hardest, and the cut fell on the summary line — a guarantee that fails on the case it exists for. Pinned by tests reading the built material: 12/08 is now carried WHOLE, and 12/05 still cuts and still declares it. A cut is therefore a CONTEXT cost, not a correctness one.

`deriveGateVerdict` is not touched: the diff reaches only the profile text, the two budget constants and one material caption. Its own tests are unmodified and green, covering every mix — `gap`/`regression` → rework, `quality` → human, `uncertain` alone → human, `uncertain` beside a finding that settled something → accept. That is the point of the fix's shape: a definition let a material limit be filed as a delivery defect, so the remedy is what the reviewer is TOLD, never how the rule reads.

npm test 1171 passed · 57 files (+4 new tests; the one existing test that changed asserted the OLD budget's cut and now asserts the carry). npm run typecheck and npm run build clean. ann check exit 0 with 0 F-AC18 lines; ann verify "clean — 0 drifts" on the live journey. And the material BUILT for 12/27 — read from buildReviewMaterial, not asserted from source — now carries "+++ b/src/store/store.ts" with no cut, which is the exact hunk its reviewer asked for by name and the whole reason this node exists; at the old budget it was dropped. The 12/27 review was NOT re-run: that gate stands at 2 of the 3 rejections the bound allows, and one more rework would put the worker out of it permanently, so the proof is the material itself, which costs no model call and burns no rejection.

findings.text: AC-1 is met: the `gap` severity entry in REVIEW_FINDINGS_MODE now reads 'the DELIVERY fails a contract requirement: the bytes are PRESENT and do not do what the criterion says, or something the criterion requires is absent FROM THE DELIVERY. Bytes the MATERIAL did not carry are NOT this…' — both halves present in one entry, and pinned by the test asserting 'the DELIVERY fails a contract requirement', 'absent FROM THE DELIVERY', 'Bytes the MATERIAL did not carry are NOT this' and 'Raise those as "uncertain"'.

AC-2 is met: the `uncertain` entry now admits settlement as well as localization — 'a real concern you cannot SETTLE: either you cannot localize it to a file and line, or the MATERIAL did not carry the bytes that would settle it (name the file the change map shows and the cut states it dropped)' — and the material's boundary caption at src/flow/review-session.ts:489 says the same at the point of use ('Raise any of them as `uncertain` … NOT as `gap` … The change map above is complete, so a file whose hunks were cut is still NAMED'). Both texts are pinned by tests reading the built material.

AC-3 is met: `DIFF_CHARS` is raised from 60000 to 180000 and `STAT_CHARS` from 4000 to 12000, each justified in its own comment from the measured distribution of this leg's 25 nodes (ten deliveries over 60,000 named with figures; 12/05's map at 4,047 against the old 4,000), and the DIFF_CHARS comment states 'A cut is therefore a CONTEXT cost, not a correctness one'. Pinned by tests reading the built material: 12/08 now carries whole with no 'chars cut', 12/05 still cuts and still declares it.

AC-4 is met: the diff touches only the profile text, the two budget constants and one material caption; `deriveGateVerdict` and its tests are unmodified (the gate-review.test.ts file is named as AC-4 evidence and the diff shows no change to it), so gap/regression still route rework, quality still routes human, uncertain still does not block.

AC-5's material half is met as far as the captured checks and the diff show: `npm test` (pass, captured at ef2f707), `npm run typecheck` (pass, captured at 9fd89aa), `npm run build` (pass, captured at 9da7a3f), `ann check` (pass, captured at 8ecce9b) and `ann verify` (clean, captured at ebab82d) are all recorded as CAPTURED FACTS; and the new test at review-session.test.ts asserting buildReviewMaterial('12-operate-loop/27-implementation-review-outcome') contains '+++ b/src/store/store.ts' with no 'chars cut' is the material-built proof the criterion names.

The new §7.4a prose states the re-measured distribution as 'ten deliveries exceeded 60,000 chars' and lists ten entries including 06-rework-visible 65,440, while the DIFF_CHARS comment in src/flow/review-session.ts and the AC-3 claim both state 'NINE of 25 deliveries exceed 60,000' and omit 06-rework-visible. The two counts disagree (nine vs ten) and one list carries an entry the other does not; the material does not carry the measurement that would settle which is correct, so AC-3's 'set from the measurement' cannot be verified as stated.

The test 'a delivery too large for ANY budget is still cut — and still says so' builds material for 12/05 and asserts the diff matches /chars cut/ and the map contains 'files changed'. It does not assert the per-file cut declaration or the map's completeness for the file whose hunks were cut, so AC-2's 'the two halves agree' on the 12/05 case rests on the test passing rather than on the material being read here; the material provided carries the test source but not the built output for 12/05, so the agreement cannot be confirmed from the bytes shown.

AC-4's 'pinned by test: the verdict for each severity mix is unchanged' is claimed against npm test, and gate-review.test.ts is named as the evidence file, but that file is CUT in the provided material (the last 23,892 of its 26,390 chars are not below). The verdict-mix assertions cannot be read here, so whether the rule is in fact unchanged is not established by the bytes shown — only by the captured npm test pass, which is a suite-level run.

The DIFF_CHARS comment claims 'This comment then set the number to 60,000 while SAYING it "carries a delivery of that size" — it did not, and it never had: the figure recorded here was 137,547.' The prior comment text is not in the reviewed diff range as a separate hunk (the diff shows the whole comment replaced), and the material does not carry the pre-change file, so the accuracy of the '137,547' figure and the claim that the old comment contradicted itself cannot be checked from the bytes provided.

§7.4a states the 12/27 incident as fact — 'the re-execution produced the same material and the same gap, so it returned rework again — two of the three rejections the bound allows, burned' — and this is the motivating case for the whole change. The reviewed range does not include the 12/27 record or its events.jsonl, so the incident's shape (two reworks, five matches, six uncertains) is asserted from prose rather than shown; if the incident differs, the rationale for the severity-text change rests on a different case than stated.

The STAT_CHARS comment states 'the widest map in the leg is 12/05's at 4,047 chars, and it was the ONLY one over the 4,000 this used to be — so the guarantee above ("still NAMED rather than invisible") was false by 47 chars on exactly the delivery whose patch is cut hardest, and the cut fell on the SUMMARY line, dropping the file count with it.' The material does not carry the pre-change map rendering for 12/05 or the 4,047 measurement, so the claim that the old budget dropped the summary line (as opposed to some other line) cannot be confirmed from the bytes shown.
